review_notes: I read the whole file. I grepped the repo and found `mellinSlope`, `mellinPeanoRemainder` and the `regIncompleteMellin_*` lemmas used only in this file. The file has no `@[simp]` lemmas and no simp-set conflicts. I saw no rewrite cycles or bad-direction rules. The one finding is a missing equation-lemma interface for the two piecewise definitions. It is a modest finding because it concerns maintainability and does not point to a simp failure. I did not run Lean, so I checked nothing about how simp behaves.

findings.problem: Both piecewise definitions have no equation lemmas for the two cases, such as `mellinSlope_zero`, `mellinSlope_of_ne`, `mellinPeanoRemainder_zero` and `mellinPeanoRemainder_of_ne`. Every use unfolds the definition by hand, either with `simp [mellinSlope, hx0]` or with `rw [mellinPeanoRemainder, ite_eq_right hx0, ...]`. These unfoldings are at lines 49, 53, 76, 80, 92, 197, 199, 225, 233 and 276. Each one unfolds the whole `if` and depends on `simp` closing the branch condition. At the `t = 0` case (lines 197 and 225) it also leaves extra `real_smul` and `zero_pow` bookkeeping. In `mellinSlope` the else-branch keeps the unreduced `slope K 0 t`. In `mellinPeanoRemainder` the else-branch keeps the `(t ^ N : ℝ)⁻¹ • (K t - taylorWithinEval ...)` form. So the normal form of an application at a nonzero point is whatever `simp [mellinX, hx0]` happens to produce.
findings.proposed_change: Add `theorem mellinPeanoRemainder_zero : mellinPeanoRemainder N a K 0 = (N.factorial : ℂ)⁻¹ * iteratedDerivWithin N K (Icc 0 a) 0 := by simp [mellinPeanoRemainder]` and `theorem mellinPeanoRemainder_of_ne (ht : t ≠ 0) : mellinPeanoRemainder N a K t = (t ^ N : ℝ)⁻¹ • (K t - taylorWithinEval K (N - 1) (Icc 0 a) 0 t) := if_neg ht`. Add the analogous `mellinSlope_zero` and `mellinSlope_of_ne`. Mark the `_zero` lemmas `@[simp]`. Use the `_of_ne` lemmas as `simp [mellinSlope_of_ne hx0]` or `rw`. Leave them out of the default simp set, because they carry a hypothesis. Then replace the ten ad-hoc unfoldings with these lemmas.
findings.benefit: The branch-specific forms are stated once and the proofs reuse them (e.g. the `hEq` and `heq` blocks). The `t = 0` value has a fixed simp normal form. The proofs no longer depend on how `simp` unfolds the `if` in each context.
